answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving one daily job slot. Whether an agent sells a lantern, appraises an opal, or writes a sonnet, the same rule applies. Creating names is free, but activating 1,000 fake sellers ties up $100,000 for a month. Splitting funds among identities creates no extra capacity: each additional slot requires another bond, making a sybil swarm costly in capital.
